subproblem.title: On a Borel subset of a coordinate n-plane, an IM orientation is a Borel sign times the coordinate n-vector (parent steps 9–10)
subproblem.statement: Assume (IMC-b) [the second conjunct of the frozen hypothesis (IMC) of the parent]: for all P, n, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R in U and every set E, if U is open and E is Borel, then there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U such that R' represents A, R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R'.mult = R.mult and R'.orient = R.orient, and (PO) [the exact frozen type of the parent's sibling Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_plane_orientation]: for all P, n, every strictly increasing ι : Fin n → Fin P, A ⊆ ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P, linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P and n-vector ξ ∈ MultiVector P n: if a_i = x_i for every a ∈ A and every i ∉ range ι, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, then either ξ(α) = α(E_ι) for every n-covector α or ξ(α) = −α(E_ι) for every α, where E_ι := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}) and e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep in U (IMRep U n), ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing, c ∈ ℝ^P, and E ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set lying in the coordinate plane through c spanned by e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}, i.e. a_i = c_i for every a ∈ E and every i ∉ range ι. Then there is a measurable σ : ℝ^P → ℤ with |σ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x such that, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E (μHE[n].restrict (R.carrier ∩ E)-a.e.), ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(E_ι) for every n-covector α.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → ∃ (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents A ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (ι : Fin n → Fin P) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P n), StrictMono ι → (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ i, (∀ j, ι j ≠ i) → a i = x i) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q → IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ α = α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ))) ∨ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ α = -α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)))) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (ι : Fin n → Fin P) (c : Euclid P) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → StrictMono ι → MeasurableSet E → (∀ a ∈ E, ∀ i, (∀ j, ι j ≠ i) → a i = c i) → ∃ σ : Euclid P → ℤ, Measurable σ ∧ (∀ x, |σ x| ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R.carrier ∩ E)), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, R.orient x α = (σ x : ℝ) * α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof ((IMC)(b) and plane_orientation give ξ = ±e_p a.e. on a face) together with the Borel sign function σ_p of step 10, read off from a strongly measurable version ξ̃ of ξ. It is stated here for any open U and any Borel set E lying in a coordinate plane. The parent applies it with U = ℝ^P and E = F̆_p.

Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, Hⁿ := μHE[n], e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), E_ι := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}).

1. (Restriction to E.) U is open and E is Borel, so (IMC-b) applied to P, n, U, R, E gives A and R' : IMRep U n with R'.carrier = M ∩ E and R'.orient = ξ; the other components are not used. Rewrite the field R'.orients with these two equalities. It says: for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q.
2. (Sign a.e.) M ∩ E is Borel (R.measurableSet_carrier, E Borel), so Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ E (ae_restrict_mem). Take x with this property and the property of step 1, together with its Q.
   - For every a ∈ M ∩ E and every i with ι(j) ≠ i for all j: a_i = c_i (as a ∈ E) and x_i = c_i (as x ∈ E), so a_i = x_i.
   - Hence (PO) applies to (P, n, ι, A := M ∩ E, x, Q, ξ(x)), using StrictMono ι. It yields: either ξ(x)(α) = α(E_ι) for every n-covector α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(E_ι) for every α.
   This holds for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x (filter_upwards over the two a.e. facts).
3. (A Borel version of ξ.) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient). Let ξ̃ := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk ξ for that field. It is strongly measurable (stronglyMeasurable_mk) and ξ = ξ̃ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (ae_eq_mk). Hence ξ = ξ̃ also holds Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e., because M ∩ E ⊆ M (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset Set.inter_subset_left).
4. (The coordinate n-vector.) Let e ∈ MultiVector P n be evaluation at E_ι: e := ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ E_ι. Then e(α) = α(E_ι) for every α, by rfl.
5. (The sign function.) Define σ(x) := 1 if ξ̃(x) = e; σ(x) := −1 if ξ̃(x) ≠ e and ξ̃(x) = −e; σ(x) := 0 otherwise.
   - |σ(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, by case analysis.
   - The sets {x : ξ̃(x) = e} and {x : ξ̃(x) = −e} are Borel, by StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun applied to ξ̃ and a constant (stronglyMeasurable_const). So σ is measurable (Measurable.ite twice, measurable_const).
   Formalization note: measurableSet_eq_fun needs TopologicalSpace.MetrizableSpace (MultiVector P n). Instance search finds T0Space but not PseudoMetrizableSpace for the operator topology. Supply it locally with a plain `have` (not `letI`), so that no second topology instance is introduced:
   have : TopologicalSpace.PseudoMetrizableSpace (MultiVector P n) := ⟨⟨(inferInstance : PseudoMetricSpace (MultiVector P n)).toUniformSpace, rfl, @EMetric.instIsCountablyGeneratedUniformity _ (inferInstance : PseudoMetricSpace (MultiVector P n)).toPseudoEMetricSpace⟩⟩
6. (Conclusion.) For Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x, both step 2 and ξ(x) = ξ̃(x) hold. Fix such an x and any α.
   (a) If ξ(x)(β) = β(E_ι) for all β, then ξ(x) = e (ContinuousLinearMap.ext and step 4). So ξ̃(x) = e and σ(x) = 1, and ξ(x)(α) = α(E_ι) = σ(x)·α(E_ι).
   (b) If ξ(x)(β) = −β(E_ι) for all β, then ξ(x) = −e (ContinuousLinearMap.ext; use the root lemma neg_apply, since ContinuousLinearMap.neg_apply is deprecated). So ξ̃(x) = −e.
      - If moreover ξ̃(x) = e, then σ(x) = 1 and ξ(x)(α) = ξ̃(x)(α) = e(α) = α(E_ι) = σ(x)·α(E_ι).
      - Otherwise ξ̃(x) ≠ e and ξ̃(x) = −e, so σ(x) = −1 and ξ(x)(α) = −α(E_ι) = σ(x)·α(E_ι).
   Hence σ is measurable with |σ| ≤ 1, and ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(E_ι) for every α, for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. x. ∎

subproblem.title: Only finitely many unit lattice faces meet a compact set (parent step 5)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. Consider index pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin k → Fin P arbitrary (not necessarily injective) and b ∈ ℤ^P. Only finitely many of them have Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} ∈ K for some y in the closed unit cube [0,1]^k. In Lean, the set {p | ∃ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) 1 ∈ K} is finite.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → {p : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) | ∃ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ) ∈ K}.Finite
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the finiteness part of step 5 of the parent proof (K is compact, so only finitely many faces meet it). The statement allows any ι, not necessarily injective, and the closed cube. So the bound on b below is ⌈ρ⌉ + k rather than the parent's ρ + 1, which relies on ι being injective. Only finiteness is used.

Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ). For p = (ι, b), Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}, so Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + S_i with S_i := Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0). Coordinate formula, used throughout: Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0). In Lean, state it as a local `have` inside the theorem (a leaf may add no separate lemma) and prove it by `simp only [PiLp.add_apply, WithLp.ofLp_sum, Finset.sum_apply, PiLp.smul_apply, PiLp.single_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero]`. Plain `simp` gets stuck on `Pi.single`, and EuclideanSpace.single_apply is deprecated in favour of PiLp.single_apply.

1. (K is bounded.) K is compact, hence bounded. So there is ρ ∈ ℝ with ‖x‖ ≤ ρ for every x ∈ K (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.exists_norm_le). For every x ∈ ℝ^P and every i, |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le).
2. (Coordinate shifts.) If y ∈ [0,1]^k, then 0 ≤ S_i ≤ k for every i. Each summand is y_j ∈ [0, 1] or 0, so it lies in [0, 1], and there are k summands (Finset.sum_nonneg, Finset.sum_le_sum, Σ_{j : Fin k} 1 = k).
3. (Bounds on b.) Let p = (ι, b) be in the set, witnessed by y ∈ [0,1]^k with x := Φ_p(y) ∈ K. For each i, |b_i + S_i| = |x_i| ≤ ρ by step 1, so −ρ ≤ b_i + S_i ≤ ρ (abs_le). Put N := ⌈ρ⌉ + k ∈ ℤ. Using ρ ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ (Int.le_ceil), 0 ≤ k and step 2:
   - b_i ≤ ρ − S_i ≤ ρ ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ ≤ N;
   - b_i ≥ −ρ − S_i ≥ −ρ − k ≥ −(⌈ρ⌉ + k) = −N.
   So b_i ∈ [−N, N] for every i; cast the real inequalities back to ℤ (exact_mod_cast). This also works when ρ < 0, for example when K = ∅.
4. (Finiteness.) By step 3 the set is contained in Set.univ ×ˢ (Set.univ.pi fun _ => Set.Icc (−N) N) ⊆ (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ). The first factor is finite (Set.finite_univ; Fin k → Fin P is a Fintype). The second is a finite product of finite integer intervals (Set.Finite.pi, Set.finite_Icc). subproblem.title: A point of the (m+1)-skeleton off the m-skeleton lies on an open unit lattice (m+1)-face (parent step 4)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P). Assume (i) x ∈ L_{m+1}: there is a finite set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∈ s; and (ii) x ∉ L_m: there is no finite set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ m + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∈ s. Then x lies on an open unit lattice (m+1)-face. That is, there are a strictly increasing ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P, b ∈ ℤ^P and y ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with 0 < y_j < 1 for every j such that x = b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)}. In Lean, with p = (ι, b): WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 = x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (x : Euclid P), (∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + 1 + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = z) → (¬ ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = z) → ∃ (p : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ)) (y : Euclid (m + 1)), StrictMono p.1 ∧ (∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ) = x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("L_n ∖ L_m is covered by open faces"; Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1), with n = m + 1 and the cardinality and coordinate bookkeeping written out.

Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ). For p = (ι, b), Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}. Coordinate formula, used throughout: Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0). In Lean, state it as a local `have` inside the theorem (a leaf may add no separate lemma) and prove it by `simp only [PiLp.add_apply, WithLp.ofLp_sum, Finset.sum_apply, PiLp.smul_apply, PiLp.single_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero]`. Plain `simp` gets stuck on `Pi.single`, and EuclideanSpace.single_apply is deprecated in favour of PiLp.single_apply.

1. (Integer coordinates.) Let J := Finset.univ.filter (fun i => ∃ z : ℤ, x_i = z) ⊆ Fin P, so i ∈ J ↔ x_i ∈ ℤ. Work classically, since this predicate is not decidable.
2. (Upper bound on P.) By (i) choose s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∈ s. Then s ⊆ J, so |s| ≤ |J| (Finset.card_le_card) and P ≤ m + 1 + |J|.
3. (Lower bound on P.) If P ≤ m + |J| held, then s := J would satisfy P ≤ m + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s, contradicting (ii). Hence m + |J| < P.
4. (Exactly m + 1 free coordinates.) By steps 2 and 3, P = m + 1 + |J|. So the complement Jᶜ in Fin P has |Jᶜ| = P − |J| = m + 1 (Finset.card_compl, Fintype.card_fin, omega).
5. (Direction map.) Let ι := Jᶜ.orderEmbOfFin h, where h : Jᶜ.card = m + 1 comes from step 4, viewed as a map Fin (m + 1) → Fin P. Then:
   - ι is strictly increasing (OrderEmbedding.strictMono), hence injective;
   - ι(j) ∈ Jᶜ, i.e. ι(j) ∉ J, for every j (Finset.orderEmbOfFin_mem);
   - every i ∉ J equals ι(j) for some j, because range ι = Jᶜ (Finset.range_orderEmbOfFin).
6. (Base point and parameters.) Put b_i := ⌊x_i⌋ (Int.floor) for every i ∈ Fin P, y := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => Int.fract (x_{ι(j)})) ∈ Euclid (m + 1), and p := (ι, b). Thus y_j = Int.fract(x_{ι(j)}).
7. (y lies in the open cube.) Int.fract(x_{ι(j)}) < 1 (Int.fract_lt_one). Since ι(j) ∉ J, x_{ι(j)} is not an integer. In particular x_{ι(j)} ≠ ⌊x_{ι(j)}⌋, so 0 < Int.fract(x_{ι(j)}). (Int.fract_pos is the equivalence 0 < fract a ↔ a ≠ ⌊a⌋; use its .2.) Hence 0 < y_j < 1 for every j.
8. (Φ_p(y) = x, coordinatewise.) Fix i ∈ Fin P. By the coordinate formula, Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋ + Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0).
   (a) If i ∈ J, then i ≠ ι(j) for every j (step 5). So every summand is 0 (Finset.sum_eq_zero) and Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋. Write x_i = z with z ∈ ℤ; then ⌊x_i⌋ = ⌊(z : ℝ)⌋ = z = x_i (Int.floor_intCast).
   (b) If i ∉ J, then i = ι(j₀) for some j₀ (step 5). Since ι is injective, the summand for every j ≠ j₀ is 0. So the sum equals y_{j₀} = Int.fract(x_i) (Finset.sum_eq_single), and Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋ + Int.fract(x_i) = x_i (Int.floor_add_fract).
   Hence Φ_p(y) = x (PiLp.ext over the coordinates).
9. (Conclusion.) p = (ι, b) and y satisfy all three requirements: StrictMono p.1 (step 5), 0 < y_j < 1 for every j (step 7) and Φ_p(y) = x (step 8). ∎

- In step 8, rewrite with the coordinate formula (the local `have`) before any `dsimp only`. Running dsimp first unfolds y j to Int.fract …, and the rewrite then fails to match.

ι := orderEmbOfFin of Jᶜ (strictly increasing, range Jᶜ), b := ⌊x⌋, y_j := fract(x_{ι(j)}) ∈ (0,1) because x_{ι(j)} ∉ ℤ.
Coordinatewise Φ_p(y)_i = ⌊x_i⌋ = x_i for i ∈ J, and ⌊x_i⌋ + fract(x_i) = x_i for i = ι(j₀); hence Φ_p(y) = x.
